ISAAC A. MING,

(Relates to CS- 2015 -066)
v.
FINAL ORDER
DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS,
Order Number: 15CS -167
Date Issued: November 16, 2015
Agency.
Isaac A. Ming, Marianna, employee representing himself.
Maria S. Dinkins, Tallahassee, attorney representing agency.
The hearing officer recommended that the Commission accept the October 26,
2015, settlement agreement of $3,583.14 in gross back pay (less all lawful deductions).
Neither party filed exceptions to the recommendation. Accordingly, the settlement
agreement is adopted as part of this order and the parties are directed to comply with it.
The case is closed.
This order may be appealed to the appropriate district court of appeal. A notice of
appeal must be received by the Commission and the district court of appeal within thirty
days from the date of this order. Except in cases of indigency, the court will require a
filing fee and the Commission will require payment for preparing the record on appeal.
Further explanation of the right to appeal is provided in Sections 120.68 and 447.504,
Florida Statutes (2015), and the Florida Rules of Appellate Procedure.

It is so ordered.
DELGADO and POOLE, Commissioners, concur.

Maria S. Dinkins, Tallahassee, attorney representing agency.
CHOPPIN, Hearing Officer.
On October 29, 2015, the parties filed a settlement agreement in this back pay
case, which I have appended to this order. Upon review, I conclude that the agreement
resolves all outstanding issues raised by Isaac A. Ming's appeal. Accordingly, I
recommend that the Commission accept the agreement, order compliance with it, and
close this case.
Any party may file exceptions to my recommended order, but exceptions must be
received by the Commission within fifteen days after the recommended order is issued.
See § 110.227(6), Fla. Stat. (2015); Fla. Admin. Code Rule 28- 106.104 and
28- 106.217(1).
ISSUED and SUBMITTED to the Public Employees Relations Commission in
accordance with Florida Administrative Code Rule 28- 106.216 and SERVED on all
parties this .26144 day of October, 2015.
SUZANNE AÒ. CHO
Hearing Officer

SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT
The parties to this action have agreed to settle this case as follows:
1. On or about September 16, 2015. the Commission issued an Order Vacating Dismissal in
the Employee's career service appeal, CS- 2015 -066, concluding the Agency did not have cause
to discipline the Employee and ordering his reinstatement. The Commission also found that the
Employee is entitled to back pay.
2. During the pendency of the PERC appeal, the Employee chose to receive his DROP
payout.
3. The Employee and the Agency agree that the back pay award shall encompass the days
that the Employee would have worked beginning May 15. 2015, the date of his Final Action
letter, and ending June 12. 2015, the date he received his DROP payout, plus statutory interest.
Specifically, the Employee would have worked on sixteen (16) days in that period of time, and
on each date, he would have worked a twelve (12) hour shift. The Employee's base rate of pay
was $18.58 per hour.
4. The Employee agrees that his signature below constitutes his acceptance of a back pay
award in the amount of $3567.36, plus statutory interest in the amount of $15.78, for a total of
$3583.14. The gross amount of $3583.14 is subject to all lawful deductions, including taxes and
appropriate allocation to his DROP account.
5. The Employee understands that in- order to process his back pay award, he is responsible
for completing a Department of Financial Services Certification of Interim Earnings and
Unemployment Benefits form and tendering the completed form to the Agency's Region i
Regional Personnel Office.
6, The Employee agrees that his signature below constitutes a settlement of the instant back
pay case and that he waives all rights to further litigation or action regarding the amount of his
back pay award

7. The Employee for himself, his attorneys, heirs, executors, administrators, successors and
assignees, does herby fully, finally, and forever release and discharge the State of Florida,
Department of Corrections and its agents, representatives, and attorneys (collectively referred to
as the "Agency"), of and froín all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, damages,
íosse.s and expenses., of any and every nature whatsoever arising from any or all of the facts or
circumstances which gave rise to this action, including, but not limited to, those claims asserted
or any federal, state, or administrative action or other claims That were or might have been
asserted by or on behalf of the Employee against the Agency, Department of Corrections, of any
other suits or charges filed with the Department of Management Services or which may be filed
by or on behalf of the Employee with any federal, state. or local agency or court whatsoever
relating to these particular facts or circumstances.
8. The parties understand that this settlement agreement is conditioned upon acceptance and
approval by the Chief Financial Officer of the Department of Financial Services.
9. The parties enter into this agreement freely and voluntarily and intend to be bound by the
terms hereof.
